title: Cap. 1 prol. IV close: word-tricks on faith; preface ends — theses next
pass_a_gloss: They are therefore mere prestiges of words, when they say that foresight faith and unbelief are conditions, not only which antecede predestination and reprobation considered commonly and promiscuously, but also from which arises the very distinction of the elect and the reprobate, and yet deny that they have any causality. For all Theologians who have ever disputed concerning the reason or cause of election presume that that obtains the force of a cause which, when posited and foresight by God, election follows; which, when denied or not foresight, election does not follow. And these are the things which I have thought should be prefaced in the place of a preface. The whole of our forthcoming disputation we will thereafter recall unto certain definite theses. Key lemmas: praestigiae verborum; causalitas; praefatio; theses.
pass_b_english: So it is mere word-trickery when they say foresight faith and unbelief are conditions — not only ones that precede predestination and reprobation taken commonly and without distinction, but ones from which the very distinction of elect and reprobate arises — and yet deny those conditions any causality. Every theologian who has ever argued the reason or cause of election assumes this: whatever, when posited and foresight by God, brings election with it, and when denied or not foresight leaves election absent, has the force of a cause. These are the points I thought should stand as a preface. From here our whole coming dispute will be drawn into certain fixed theses.
source_text: Sunt ergo merae verborum praestigiae, cum aiunt praevisam fidem & infidelitatem esse conditiones, non modo quae antecedunt praedestinationem & reprobationem communiter & promiscue consideratam, sed etiam ex quibus oritur ipsa distinctio electorum & reprobatorum, & tamen negant habere aliquam causalitatem. Nam omnes Theologi qui unquam disputarunt de ratione aut causa electionis, praesumunt id vim causae obtinere, qua posita & a Deo praevisa sequitur; qua negata aut non praevisa non sequitur electio. Atque haec ea sunt quae praefationis loco praemittenda putavi. Totam, quae futura est, disputationem nostram deinceps ad certas quasdam theses revocabimus.
